message: All food-contact packaging materials must comply with FSSAI Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Regulations, 2018.
Total migration of packaging constituents into food must not exceed 10 mg/dm2.
regulation_citation: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018, Regulation 5; BIS IS 10190
source: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018, Regulation 5; BIS IS 10190

message: Lead content in packaging material must not exceed 1.0 mg/kg.
Recycled plastic used for food packaging must meet food-grade safety standards.
LDPE may swell or allow excessive migration when in contact with fatty foods. Use PP or PET instead.
regulation_citation: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018, Regulation 4; BIS IS 10190
source: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018, Regulation 4; BIS IS 10190

message: Acidic foods (pH < 4.5) may accelerate migration from certain plastics. Use glass, PET, or PP as alternatives.
Hot-fill products (above 70°C) require packaging rated for the filling temperature. PP and HDPE are suitable; LDPE may deform.
Retort processing (above 120°C) requires retort-grade laminates (PET/Al/PP). Standard laminates will fail.
Plastic packaging requires Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) registration under Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016.
regulation_citation: Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016, Rule 4(1); EPR Guidelines 2022
source: Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016, Rule 4(1); EPR Guidelines 2022

message: Plastic packaging must display the recycling symbol and resin identification code.
Single-use plastic packaging below 50 microns thickness is restricted. Ensure minimum thickness compliance.
Fresh dairy products (milk, paneer) require packaging that supports cold chain and has adequate oxygen barrier.
regulation_citation: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018, Regulation 4; FSSAI Dairy Regulations 2011
source: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018, Regulation 4; FSSAI Dairy Regulations 2011

message: Meat and fish require MAP or vacuum packaging with high oxygen barrier (OTR < 5 cc/m2/day) for adequate shelf life.
regulation_citation: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018, Regulation 4; FSSAI Meat Products Order
source: FSSAI Packaging Regulations 2018, Regulation 4; FSSAI Meat Products Order

message: High-fat foods (fat > 20%) may cause stress cracking in certain plastics. Use PP, PET, or glass.
Aluminium foil laminates provide the best barrier but are not recyclable. Consider EPR implications.
regulation_citation: Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016; EPR Guidelines 2022
source: Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016; EPR Guidelines 2022

message: Biodegradable plastics must be certified by BIS (IS 17088) to claim biodegradability. Misleading claims are prohibited.
Inks and adhesives used on food packaging must be food-safe and must not migrate into food.
Secondary and transport packaging need not be food-grade but must not contaminate primary packaging.
Dry grains and pulses must be packaged at moisture content below critical limits to prevent mould growth.
regulation_citation: FSSAI Licensing Regulations 2011, Schedule 4; BIS standards for grains
source: FSSAI Licensing Regulations 2011, Schedule 4; BIS standards for grains

message: Packaging material must be rated for the intended storage and transport temperature range.
